cold-reader.reconstruction: Intended behavior: a customer requests a record export. The system calls GET /exports/create with no request ID, using the existing export API (proposal.md Impact; spec.md Requirement 'Create export'). The export is a JSON document with customer ID and display name fields (design.md, sole paragraph), covering the authenticated customer profile (spec.md). Access is restricted to the requesting customer. On success, the synchronous response returns a download link for that customer's profile (spec.md Scenario 'Request succeeds'; design.md). Links expire after one hour, and the underlying files are deleted at expiry (design.md). Failure handling: timeouts are retried twice with one second between attempts; after the retries are exhausted, the user sees a terminal failure with a retry button. Authentication failures are terminal (design.md). A user retry creates a new logical request (design.md). In scope: export creation, bounded retry, terminal failure, and user retry (proposal.md What Changes; tasks.md 1.1). Acceptance evidence named in tasks.md 1.1: authenticated success, retries, terminal failure, and user retry. The only spec scenario is the success path (spec.md). Decisions an implementer must invent: the per-attempt timeout duration; whether 'twice' means two total attempts or two retries after an initial attempt; which failures count as timeouts (only timeouts, or also 5xx and network errors); the error message text and whether the auth-failure state also shows the retry button; the exact field list of the 'customer profile' versus the two fields named in design.md; how an expired link is answered; and how duplicate server-side exports from automatic retries are handled, given that no request ID is sent.

evidence.reference: Whole document (single paragraph, no section headings)
Why; What Changes; Capabilities; Impact sections
Purpose; ADDED Requirements 'Create export'; Scenario 'Request succeeds'

findings.location: specs/export/spec.md: ADDED Requirements and Scenario 'Request succeeds'; tasks.md: 1.1
findings.scenario: tasks.md 1.1 requires verifying authenticated success, retries, terminal failure, and user retry, and design.md defines the auth-failure, expiry, and access-restriction behavior. The spec contains only one requirement and one success scenario.
findings.impact: Retry, terminal-failure, auth-failure, expiry, and access-restriction behavior have no normative requirement or testable scenario, so acceptance of those behaviors cannot be checked against the spec.
findings.resolution: spec.md contains a requirement and at least one WHEN/THEN scenario each for bounded retry, terminal failure with retry button, authentication failure, user retry creating a new request, one-hour link expiry with file deletion, and requesting-customer-only access.

findings.location: design.md: retry paragraph ('Retry timeouts twice with one second between attempts')
findings.scenario: An implementer reads 'retry twice' and must choose between two total attempts and three total attempts (one initial plus two retries). The per-attempt timeout duration is also unspecified.
findings.impact: Different implementations will make a different number of calls and wait different durations before failing. Retry tests cannot assert a single correct attempt count or timing.
findings.resolution: design.md states the total attempt count, the per-attempt timeout duration, and the delay schedule.

findings.location: design.md: 'Retry timeouts twice' and 'Authentication failures are terminal'
findings.scenario: A failure other than a timeout or authentication failure occurs, such as a 5xx response, a network reset, or a malformed response. The design does not say whether it is retried, treated as terminal, or handled differently.
findings.impact: Implementers will classify error types differently, so retry behavior and terminal-failure display will vary across implementations.
findings.resolution: design.md lists every error class that is retried, every class that is terminal, and the handling for any unlisted class.

findings.location: design.md: 'Retry timeouts twice' combined with 'User retry creates a new logical request' and 'no request ID'
findings.scenario: The system performs an automatic retry after a timeout where the first attempt actually created an export on the server. Because GET /exports/create carries no request ID, the retry has no way to identify the original request.
findings.impact: Duplicate exports may be created for one user action. The design does not say whether duplicates are acceptable, whether the server deduplicates, or whether only the first created link is returned.
findings.resolution: design.md states the duplicate-export policy for automatic retries and whether the user sees one link or several.

findings.location: specs/export/spec.md: 'Create export' ('a JSON export of the authenticated customer profile') versus design.md ('JSON fields are customer ID and display name')
findings.scenario: The spec describes the full authenticated customer profile, while the design lists only two fields. An implementer cannot tell whether the export must contain every profile field or only customer ID and display name.
findings.impact: The export payload may over-include personal data or omit fields that acceptance tests expect.
findings.resolution: spec.md or design.md enumerates the exact JSON fields included in the export, and the spec and design agree on that list.

findings.location: design.md: 'links expire after one hour and files are deleted then'
findings.scenario: A customer opens a download link after one hour has passed. The design does not say what status or message the link returns, nor whether deletion is immediate at expiry or is a later cleanup job.
findings.impact: Expiry and deletion behavior cannot be tested precisely, and the client will not know whether to offer a new export.
findings.resolution: design.md or spec.md defines the response for expired links and whether deletion occurs at exactly one hour or within a stated grace period.

findings.location: design.md: 'GET /exports/create' versus proposal.md 'Use existing export API' and spec.md 'through the existing export API'
findings.scenario: The design specifies a GET request that creates a resource. The packet does not confirm that the existing export API exposes this endpoint or method, so the design's endpoint may conflict with the existing API.
findings.impact: If the existing API uses a different method or path, the implementer must choose between the design and the existing API, and the chosen behavior may not match what the proposal promises.
findings.resolution: design.md confirms that GET /exports/create is the existing export API endpoint and method, or it names the correct endpoint and method.

evidence.reference: whole file (Requirement: Create export, Scenario: Request succeeds)

findings.location: design.md: Use GET /exports/create with no request ID; contract.md line 2
findings.scenario: Implementation follows design.md and issues GET /exports/create. The existing API contract states POST /exports creates an export and GET /exports/create is unsupported.
findings.impact: Every export request fails against the existing API, so the core capability cannot work. The design's stated endpoint and method are inconsistent with the repository's documented contract.
findings.resolution: design.md names the method and path that contract.md documents as supported (POST /exports), or the planning packet cites an authoritative source showing the contract has changed and contract.md is updated. The spec and tasks reference the same endpoint.

findings.location: design.md: Use GET /exports/create with no request ID; Failure handling retry sentence; contract.md line 2
findings.scenario: A timeout occurs and the client retries twice. Because design.md specifies no request ID, each attempt is sent as a new logical request. The contract requires a unique request ID per logical request, reused on timeout retries, to avoid duplicate writes.
findings.impact: Timeout retries can create duplicate export writes. The retry policy is unsafe under the documented contract.
findings.resolution: design.md specifies that a request ID is generated once per logical request, reused across timeout retries, and regenerated only for user retry. The spec or design states this, and tasks.md 1.1 verifies that retries reuse the same ID.

findings.location: design.md: Synchronous response returns the link on success; specs/export/spec.md: Scenario Request succeeds
findings.scenario: Design says the response is synchronous and returns the link, while the contract only documents POST /exports creating an export with no response shape. The spec's success scenario only says a link is returned, with no stated status or sync/async behaviour.
findings.impact: Implementers may assume an asynchronous job model and poll, or a synchronous link and not handle the 'in progress' case. Timeout and retry behaviour depends on which model holds, so the retry rules in design.md are not well defined.
findings.resolution: The spec states the response model (synchronous or not) and the success and timeout response shape, cross-referenced to the existing export API contract.

findings.resolution: specs/export/spec.md contains requirements and scenarios for: timeout retry count and interval; terminal failure and retry affordance; user retry as a new logical request; authentication failure as terminal; link expiry of one hour with file deletion; and access restricted to the requesting customer. adjudicator.reconstruction: Intended behavior: a customer requests a JSON record export through the existing export API (proposal.md Impact). The design calls GET /exports/create with no request ID (design.md line 3), but the repository contract documents POST /exports as the creating endpoint, with GET /exports/create unsupported, and requires a unique request ID per logical request, reused on timeout retries (contract.md line 2). On success the synchronous response returns a download link (design.md line 3; spec.md Scenario 'Request succeeds'). Timeouts are retried twice with one-second spacing, then a terminal failure with a retry button is shown; authentication failures are terminal; a user retry is a new logical request (design.md line 3). Links expire after one hour and files are deleted at that point; access is limited to the requesting customer (design.md line 3). The spec contains only one requirement and one success scenario (spec.md lines 8-13), while tasks.md 1.1 requires verifying authenticated success, retries, terminal failure, and user retry (tasks.md line 4). Reviewer 2 returned an empty reconstruction; this adjudicator reconstructs the intended behavior from the artifacts directly.

findings.reason: Same evidence and same resolution as C1 (spec.md lines 8-13 versus tasks.md line 4 and design.md line 3). C1 is canonical. A4 adds no unique requirement beyond C1's resolution.

findings.impact: The spec permits exporting the full profile, which could include fields beyond ID and display name, with privacy consequences.
findings.resolution: specs/export/spec.md lists the exact exported fields consistently with design.md, or design.md and the spec both reference the same field definition.

findings.location: design.md line 3 ('show a terminal failure and a retry button' and 'Authentication failures are terminal')
findings.scenario: Design line 3 says the retry button appears after timeout exhaustion, and separately that authentication failures are terminal. It does not say whether the authentication-failure state shows the retry button or what error message text is displayed.
findings.impact: Two implementers could render the auth-failure state differently, with or without a retry button and with different messages. The effect is localized to UI state.
findings.resolution: design.md states whether the authentication-failure terminal state shows the retry button and what user-facing message is shown for each terminal state.
findings.reason: New finding. Verified against design.md line 3: the retry-button rule is tied to timeout exhaustion, and the auth-failure display is unspecified.
